autonomous_processes: Outside a trial, the oscilloscope is redrawn continuously and its scanline and jack signal bars animate without changing the qualification state.

After TEST THIS LINE, the selected carrier's target phase drifts continuously at a generated rate of 2.0-2.2 phase steps per second; the amber candidate waveform changes relative to the cyan reference.
A 100 ms sampling timer records alignment and lock history, updates the visible lock/progress state, and ends the trial at 6400 ms for the 45-sample and final 12-of-14 checks.
grouped_control_modes: Incoming-jack selection across all generated switchboards and attempts.
Full phase-slider tuning before and during every lock trial (the common witness mode D).
Full shape-slider tuning before and during every lock trial.
Lock-test start and administrative reissue after a failed attempt.

clause_i.reason: For the common within-trial phase-slider value mode, identical action histories can lead to different generated phase offsets or drift signs. The delayed phase-slider value that maximizes lock differs across those visible states, so no q(I_t) works for every still-salvageable history.

clause_ii.reason: The five-frame, 600 ms window visibly records the changing amber/cyan phase relation. A bounded-window policy can infer the current error and drift direction/magnitude and choose the phase-slider value for the state at delayed delivery.

clause_iii.reason: The selected carrier drifts at 2.0-2.2 phase steps per second during the 6400 ms trial. During a 300 ms no-action interval, a phase-slider value aligned at t is stale at t+300 ms and has lower alignment/lock advantage, while enough trial remains for a corrective action. The loss is caused by carrier-state drift, not a deadline or the decorative idle animation.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: The common witness is the selected carrier during its lock trial: elapsed drift shifts the amber waveform against the cyan reference, and the phase-slider value remains active while sampling proceeds every 100 ms. That one drift process supplies the bounded visual prediction problem and makes a stale phase action lose value.

pre_run.reason: Only the zero-distortion target can lock. With the exact skew and any fixed phase, the continuous interval inside the 0.85-step phase tolerance has length at most 2*0.85/2.0 = 0.85 seconds, because every target drift magnitude is at least 2.0 steps per second. Sampling every 100 ms can therefore yield at most 9 locked samples, far below the required 45, so a no-update trial cannot succeed for any generated instance. The pre-run threshold is not met and the mathematical witness remains label yes.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 has 8 lines, drift magnitudes 2.0-2.2 steps per second, 0.85-step phase tolerance, 6400 ms trial, and 45/12 lock quotas.
Full sliders and the shared 600 ms, 5-frame observation schedule are configured.
Each generated line receives a phase offset, skew offset, nonzero selected drift value, and exactly one line receives zero distortion.
The generated target is the zero-distortion line, and qualification exposes phase tolerance, trial duration, sampling, and lock quotas.
Target phase depends on elapsed trial time and drift, and lock residual combines phase, skew, and distortion errors.
The visible amber candidate waveform is rendered with elapsed drift against the cyan reference on the live canvas.
Jack and test controls are disabled during a trial while tuning still updates phase or skew and records the input source.
The trial samples alignment on the configured interval and checks total and final lock quotas at the configured duration.
The authoritative replay uses the same elapsed-time drift and residual threshold.
The controlled grader distinguishes full slider tuning input.
The grader replays sample timing and requires the configured total and final lock quotas on the target line.
The implementation solver repeatedly estimates elapsed target phase and corrects it through the full slider during the live trial; this is implementation evidence of active tracking.
